claim: The drone that hit a car in Lithuania on 18 October entered from Poland
claimed_by: Lithuania (president and prime minister)
evidence: Lithuanian radar track with a minute-by-minute timeline
conflict: Poland says its radars show no crossing. Ukraine says Russian jamming may have diverted it. Russian outlet EADaily spins it as Lithuania letting Ukrainian drones through.
verdict_note: Most likely a stray Ukrainian drone. Two NATO allies disagree on its route.

claim: The Pentagon asked the Baltic states to tone down their rhetoric on Russia
claimed_by: Reuters (four anonymous sources)
conflict: Pentagon declined to comment but did not deny. Baltic ministries silent.
verdict_note: Credible but not confirmed on the record.

claim: Russia could make a limited attack on a NATO country in the coming months
claimed_by: Danish intelligence (25 September); US intelligence via WSJ and CNN (August)
conflict: Estonia's intelligence service: no intention to attack NATO this year. Putin: no plans to attack.
verdict_note: Services disagree on the odds but agree the risk is low and growing. Hybrid escalation is the more likely path.

claim: Russia is adding 16,000–20,000 military hospital beds near the Baltic states
claimed_by: Militarnyi, citing anonymous sources in Russian media; amplified by others
conflict: No official or imagery confirmation. Beds are also planned around Moscow and Smolensk, which fits Ukraine casualties.
verdict_note: Single source; headlines saying beds are moving 'close to the Baltics' overstate it.

claim: Belarus is preparing infrastructure for a Russian push to the Suwałki Gap by spring 2027
claimed_by: BELPOL (exiled Belarusian security officers)
conflict: No official confirmation or denial.
verdict_note: Plausible but partisan. Watch for imagery of rail and communications works.

claim: Ships at Baltiysk signal a Kaliningrad build-up for an attack
claimed_by: YouTube commentary channels
evidence: Imagery shows equipment being loaded out
conflict: OSINT analysts and Militarnyi: destination unknown; the same ships have supplied Africa before.
verdict_note: The imagery is real; the framing is not supported by it.

claim: NATO is preparing an air and naval blockade of Kaliningrad
claimed_by: Russian embassies and a diplomatic note to NATO (late September)
conflict: NATO replied that none of its exercises threaten Russian territory.
verdict_note: No evidence offered. Reads as a pretext narrative backing nuclear warnings.

claim: The Pentagon asked the Baltic states to tone down their rhetoric on Russia
claimed_by: Reuters (four anonymous sources)
conflict: Estonia's foreign minister: no official US proposal. Estonia's PM: allies are asking Estonia to hold back. Peskov: reports should be taken with a grain of salt. Pentagon declines to comment. Lithuania and Latvia silent.
verdict_note: Still unconfirmed on the record, but Estonian reactions suggest informal pressure rather than a formal request.

claim: Russian intelligence was behind the Starlink arson attacks in Poland, Bulgaria and Lithuania
claimed_by: Poland's intelligence minister; Lithuania's prime minister; Der Spiegel
evidence: Official statements; arrests in four countries; press reports on the gang leader's protection in Russia
conflict: Lithuanian police say the ultimate motive has not been established. German broadcaster ARD notes that gang membership is hard to establish. Russia routinely denies such accusations.
verdict_note: The cross-border link is official; the Russian tasking is asserted by officials but not yet shown in court.

claim: Russia will demand a NATO pullback to 1997 lines in peace talks
claimed_by: The Telegraph (unnamed diplomatic sources)
conflict: Not announced by the Kremlin. The Kremlin ruled out European participation in the Abu Dhabi round on 29 October, while the report says Moscow wants Europeans at the table.
verdict_note: Plausible given Russia's 2021 demands, but a single anonymous-source report.

claim: The Kaliningrad blackout was caused by a protection system tripping at the CHP-2 power plant
claimed_by: Kaliningrad regional authorities; grid operator Rosseti
conflict: Ukrainian outlets say the cause could not be verified; social media posts speculated about sabotage without evidence.
verdict_note: The official explanation is plausible and not contradicted by any evidence, but it has not been independently verified.

claim: Russia does not want a war with Europe
claimed_by: Putin (29 October)
conflict: Danish and US intelligence see a low but growing risk of a limited test of NATO; European officials blame Russia for an ongoing sabotage campaign.
verdict_note: Statements of intent cannot be verified; the hybrid record runs against the reassurance.

claim: Belarus is relaying signals for Russian attack drones
claimed_by: Ukraine's border guard spokesperson and military intelligence chief; Ukrainian monitoring project E-radar
conflict: Minsk has not responded. No NATO or Lithuanian technical body has confirmed it. Ukrainian explanations (commercial LTE networks or purpose-built relays) differ.
verdict_note: Relevant to the Baltics because a Russian Gerbera drone was shot down over Lithuania in September; all sources are Ukrainian or Belarusian opposition.

claim: The US is pressing Lithuania to allow Belarusian potash transit despite EU sanctions
claimed_by: Politico (four anonymous European officials)
conflict: Lithuanian PM said in September no US request had been received. The State Department did not respond. Lithuanian officials reject the idea on the record.
verdict_note: Consistent with earlier reporting of US outreach to Minsk; the request itself is not on the record.

claim: The Pentagon asked the Baltic states to tone down their rhetoric on Russia
claimed_by: Reuters (four anonymous sources)
conflict: Lithuania's defence minister says he has no information about such a request. Estonia's PM says no such complaints reached him directly; Estonia's foreign minister and ministry secretary general know of no official request. Pentagon and NATO decline to comment. Latvia silent.
verdict_note: Moved from Likely: two governments now say on the record that no request reached them, though they deny only official or direct requests and Reuters described informal ones.

claim: Russia will demand a NATO pullback to 1997 lines in peace talks
claimed_by: The Telegraph (unnamed diplomatic sources); ISW says the Kremlin has renewed this demand
conflict: ISW's statement cites its own earlier assessments, not a new primary Russian statement. The Kremlin wants Europeans excluded from the talks, while the Telegraph says Moscow wants them at the table.
verdict_note: Consistent with Russia's long-standing 2021 position, but no Russian official has been shown making it as a formal demand in the current talks.

claim: The Belarusian government organises illegal migration into the Baltic states
claimed_by: Estonian and Latvian interior ministers (30 October)
conflict: Minsk has not responded in the available reporting; it has denied such accusations in the past. Armed, masked escorts at Latvia's border in early October support the claim.
verdict_note: Consistent with years of official findings in Poland, Lithuania and Latvia, though direct proof of state direction is rarely published.

claim: A Russian national arrested in Świdnica was gathering rail intelligence for a foreign service
claimed_by: Polish police and prosecutors
conflict: The intelligence service has not been named and the charge has not been tested in court. No Russian response reported.
verdict_note: A formal charge backed by seized material, but still an accusation; the suspect is presumed innocent.

claim: Men are being seized off the streets in Russian cities and pressed to sign army contracts
claimed_by: Meduza, iStories, Verstka; relatives and rights groups
conflict: No official confirmation or response from Russian authorities in the reporting. Most accounts are second-hand.
verdict_note: Several independent outlets and complaints from many regions point the same way.

claim: Russia wants fully-fledged relations with European countries
claimed_by: Putin (29 October)
conflict: Moscow simultaneously demands that European leaders stay out of peace talks, and European governments blame Russia for an ongoing sabotage campaign.
verdict_note: A statement of intent that cannot be verified and that Russia's hybrid record contradicts.

claim: Belarusian state structures may be coordinating sabotage in Europe alongside Russian intelligence
claimed_by: Robert Lansing Institute (commentary)
conflict: The piece itself says state complicity is not established; the only fact behind it is that two suspects detained in Germany are Belarusian citizens. German prosecutors have not named a client.
verdict_note: A hypothesis from an outlet that does not disclose its funding; no official or evidence-based source supports Belarusian state involvement.

claim: The object that entered eastern Latvia on 1 November was a stray Ukrainian drone
claimed_by: Implied by Izvestia's headline and related links; Latvian armed forces call it only an unidentified object
conflict: Latvia has named neither the type nor the origin. The Kyiv Independent says it was likely a drone of unclear origin. Earlier stray drones over Latvia were both Ukrainian and Russian.
verdict_note: No official identification yet; the object left toward Russia, which by itself proves nothing about where it came from.

claim: The Pentagon asked the Baltic states to tone down their rhetoric on Russia
claimed_by: Reuters (four anonymous sources)
conflict: Lithuania's defence minister and Estonia's PM say no such request reached them; Estonia's foreign ministry knows of no official request. A former Estonian diplomat now argues the message should be more measured anyway. Pentagon silent.
verdict_note: No new evidence either way; the Estonian debate is about style, not about whether a request was made.

claim: Russia is building an over-the-horizon radar near Gvardeysk that could watch NATO aircraft across much of Europe
claimed_by: ICEYE imagery via FAZ and Stars and Stripes; amplified by the Robert Lansing Institute
conflict: The construction is visible on imagery, but the range and purpose are projections, and whether it is operational is unknown. No Russian or NATO comment.
verdict_note: Construction is well supported by imagery; the capability claims are not yet confirmed.

claim: Russia is plotting to kill European defence-industry executives
claimed_by: Representatives of five EU intelligence agencies (to the Financial Times), summarised by Al Jazeera
conflict: No named official or court case in the reporting describes a specific plot. Moscow denies running sabotage in Europe.
verdict_note: Consistent with earlier reported plots and with incendiary devices found at Munich offices, but the central claim rests on unnamed officials.

claim: Russia will demand a NATO pullback to 1997 lines in peace talks
claimed_by: The Telegraph (unnamed diplomatic sources); ISW says the Kremlin has renewed this demand
conflict: ISW's 31 October assessment again cites the demand without a fresh primary Russian statement. No Russian official has been shown making it as a formal demand in the current talks.
verdict_note: No new evidence since yesterday; consistent with Russia's 2021 position but still unconfirmed as a demand in talks.

claim: Armed groups could try to cross from Kaliningrad into Poland in the coming days
claimed_by: RMF, citing unnamed sources on warnings from Poland's Military Intelligence Service and allied agencies
conflict: The police chief confirmed on the record only a general sabotage threat and did not mention armed groups. Authorities call the operation preventive; no incident has been reported. No Russian response found.
verdict_note: The operation is real; the specific armed-incursion scenario rests on anonymous sources.

claim: A Russian citizen deported from Estonia kept contacts with Russian intelligence officers
claimed_by: Estonia's Internal Security Service (KAPO)
conflict: KAPO has not published its evidence and the case has not been tested in court. No public response from the man or from Moscow found.
verdict_note: An on-the-record claim by a security service with a strong track record, but the evidence is not public.

claim: The object that entered eastern Latvia on 1 November was a stray Ukrainian drone
claimed_by: Implied by Izvestia's headline and related links; Latvian armed forces call it only an unidentified object
conflict: Latvia still names neither type nor origin. Its interceptor self-destructed without reaching the object, so there is no wreckage to examine. Earlier stray drones over Latvia were both Ukrainian and Russian.
verdict_note: No new evidence on origin; the exit toward Russia by itself proves nothing.

claim: Russian electronic warfare pushed the drone that fell in Lithuania on 18 October off course
claimed_by: Ukraine's foreign ministry spokesperson, as reported by European Pravda
conflict: Lithuania says the drone came in from Poland and carried explosives; Ukraine expressed regret, implying it was Ukrainian, and blamed Russian jamming. No independent technical finding on the cause has been published.
verdict_note: Plausible given persistent Russian jamming in the region, but it is the explanation of the drone's operator, not an independent finding.

claim: The people seen with flashlights near Sępopol were attempting a Russian provocation
claimed_by: Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk, hedged: he said this was so 'if that was the intention'
conflict: Nobody crossed the border and no one has been identified. Tusk himself said he could not be fully certain. Russia's embassy calls the sabotage warnings fake; no Russian comment on the incident itself.
verdict_note: The sighting is confirmed; its purpose is not.

claim: Polish and allied intelligence warned of possible incursions by armed people from Kaliningrad in the first half of November
claimed_by: Donald Tusk on the record; earlier RMF citing unnamed sources; AP says warnings came from Polish, NATO, Ukrainian and US services
conflict: Yesterday this rested on anonymous sources; the prime minister has now confirmed the content of the warnings on the record. The underlying intelligence is not public, and Russia dismisses it as fake.
verdict_note: That the warnings were given is now well established; whether such an incursion was really planned cannot be judged from public evidence.

claim: The drone that entered eastern Latvia on 1 November was a Russian Geran
claimed_by: Latvia's armed forces (most likely assessment); earlier, Izvestia's framing implied a stray Ukrainian drone
conflict: The drone flew back into Russia and no wreckage exists, so the assessment rests on tracking data. Russian state media had linked the alert to Ukrainian drones; no Russian official has commented on Latvia's new assessment.
verdict_note: An on-the-record military assessment; it outweighs the earlier implication of a Ukrainian origin, which had no evidence behind it.

claim: The drone over Balvi on 3 November was Ukrainian
claimed_by: Latvia's armed forces, on initial visual identification
conflict: Latvia says the exact type and origin are not established, and the wreckage has not been found. Ukraine has not commented.
verdict_note: Plausible, given Ukraine's attacks on Russian Baltic ports, but provisional until wreckage is found.

claim: Polish warnings about possible sabotage are fake news driven by militarist rhetoric
claimed_by: Russia's embassy in Warsaw, via TASS
conflict: Several services, according to Tusk and AP, issued the warnings independently. Poland has not published the evidence, but Russia offers none for its denial either.
verdict_note: A blanket denial with no evidence, from a government whose earlier denials of sabotage in Poland were contradicted by Polish investigations.

claim: The people seen with flashlights near Sępopol were attempting a Russian provocation
claimed_by: Implied by Donald Tusk; Polish and Ukrainian media headlines
conflict: Tusk said he could not be certain; Siemoniak said he could not confirm the warned plan involved crossing from Kaliningrad. Russia calls the warnings fake. No further details have been released.
verdict_note: The sighting is real; its purpose remains unknown, and no new evidence has emerged.

claim: Polish and allied intelligence warned of possible incursions by armed people from Kaliningrad in the first half of November
claimed_by: Donald Tusk on the record; Stars and Stripes names NATO commander Alexus Grynkewich among those who warned; Tomasz Siemoniak
conflict: Several officials confirm the warnings were given, but Siemoniak calls them imprecise. The underlying intelligence is not public, and Russia dismisses it as fake.
verdict_note: That the warnings were given is well established; whether an incursion was really planned cannot be judged from public evidence.

claim: A planned provocation on the Kaliningrad border would be staged so that Ukrainians are blamed
claimed_by: Tomasz Siemoniak, Polish minister coordinating special services (TVN24)
conflict: No evidence has been published, and the minister himself called the information imprecise. Russian outlets have long pushed narratives that blame Ukraine for incidents in Poland and the Baltics, which makes the scenario plausible but not proven.
verdict_note: A serious official warning about possible intent, not evidence of an operation.

claim: Russian intelligence was behind the 23 September arson at a Starlink ground station near Warsaw
claimed_by: Polish government; Der Spiegel reporting on the investigation
conflict: Arrests in Germany and charges in several countries back the criminal case, but the Russian link rests on Polish attribution and press reports of a Turkish crime group that may have worked for Russian services. Russia has not commented on this case.
verdict_note: Consistent with a well-documented pattern of Russian proxy sabotage, but not yet proven in court.

claim: Poland's Kaliningrad border operation is a political distraction from Tusk's domestic troubles
claimed_by: RT (Russian state media); earlier the Russian embassy in Warsaw
conflict: The warnings came from several allied services, including NATO's commander, and US and German forces have separately tightened their own security. RT offers no evidence for its motive claim.
verdict_note: A motive claim with no supporting evidence that ignores the allied sources of the warnings.

claim: NATO is an aggressive bloc preparing for war with Russia, while Russia and Belarus intend to attack no one
claimed_by: Alexander Lukashenko at the Minsk security conference (Izvestia)
conflict: NATO's public plans are built around deterring and repelling an attack. Lithuania's threat assessment judges that Russia could in the longer term carry out limited operations against NATO states, and Russia gave similar assurances before invading Ukraine in 2022.
verdict_note: Turns allied defensive preparations into proof of aggression and offers assurances contradicted by recent history.

claim: Poland and the Baltic states are training people to work for Russia's collapse from within
claimed_by: Sergei Shoigu, Secretary of Russia's Security Council; echoed by Maria Zakharova
conflict: No evidence offered. Poland, Lithuania, Germany and Romania have published arrests and court cases showing the reverse flow: people recruited by Russian services for spying and sabotage in Europe.
verdict_note: A mirror-image accusation with no evidence, timed after Polish and Lithuanian disclosures.

claim: Three Ukrainians in Lithuania carried out paid tasks for hostile foreign intelligence services
claimed_by: Lithuania's State Security Department (VSD)
conflict: The VSD did not name the services, open a criminal case or publish evidence; the three cannot contest it in Lithuania now that they have left. The method described matches earlier proven cases.
verdict_note: A credible official finding matching a known pattern, but untested in court and with the sponsor unnamed.

claim: Six people detained in Poland supplied Russia with military components, and four spied for Russia
claimed_by: Polish Internal Security Agency (ABW); minister Tomasz Siemoniak
conflict: Backed by searches and a court custody order; details of the evidence are not public. No Russian response.
verdict_note: An active criminal case with judicial oversight; guilt not yet established.

claim: A man living in Russia coordinated a 2024 plot to attack Romanian oil and gas sites
claimed_by: Romanian anti-terrorism prosecutors (DIICOT); Bucharest Court of Appeals
conflict: The hired accomplice was convicted in 2025, which supports the plot itself; the coordinator's role and the Russian connection rest on the prosecution's case, as he is beyond Romania's reach.
verdict_note: The plot is established in court; the coordinator's guilt and the sponsorship are not yet tested.

claim: Polish and allied intelligence warned of possible incursions by armed people from Kaliningrad in the first half of November
claimed_by: Donald Tusk; Tomasz Siemoniak; NATO commander Alexus Grynkewich (per Stars and Stripes)
conflict: No confirmed crossing attempt since the warnings; Poland's operation continues until at least 8 November. Russia calls the warnings fake and Shoigu now accuses Poland itself of training saboteurs.
verdict_note: That the warnings were given is well established; whether an incursion was planned cannot be judged from public evidence.

claim: GPS interference affected almost all of NATO's eastern flank on 3 November
claimed_by: ItaMilRadar (OSINT), reported by Militarnyi
conflict: Flight-data maps show where aircraft lose accuracy, not who is jamming; part of the interference stems from the war in Ukraine. Baltic governments have long attributed the Kaliningrad-area interference to Russia.
verdict_note: The pattern is well documented; this single map adds a snapshot, not new attribution.

claim: A Russian satellite rehearsed an attack on a Finnish ICEYE radar satellite
claimed_by: Greg Gillinger (Integrity ISR) via Reuters; supported in tone by US Under Secretary Thomas DiNanno; repeated by the Robert Lansing Institute
conflict: Orbital data confirm unusual close approaches, but Germany's space commander says they could be inspection or interference and do not prove an attack plan; the Lansing piece itself says the data do not show preparations for a strike. Reported distances range from 26 metres to about a kilometre. Russia has not commented.
verdict_note: The manoeuvres are documented; the 'rehearsal' reading is plausible but not established.

claim: The Fitburg's officers damaged Finland–Estonia undersea cables with the ship's anchor
claimed_by: Helsinki District Court; Finnish prosecutors
conflict: A first-instance conviction for aggravated criminal damage; an appeal is possible. The court did not find that the Russian state ordered it, and a separate court dismissed charges in the Eagle S case in October.
verdict_note: Tested in court, but not final, and state direction is not established.

claim: US officials pressed Lithuania to allow Belarusian fertiliser transit through Klaipėda
claimed_by: Politico (relayed by LRT)
conflict: A presidential adviser did not deny an approach but called the report outdated; Foreign Minister Kęstutis Budrys denied that any such discussion is taking place. No US comment reported.
verdict_note: An approach may have happened, but the Lithuanian accounts differ and current talks are denied.

claim: Satellite data show Russia partly replenishing self-propelled artillery near Petrozavodsk, about 185 km from Finland
claimed_by: Robert Lansing Institute (citing an 'OCP monitoring system')
conflict: No official, imagery publisher or quality outlet has confirmed it; the source of the data is not identified. The same piece says no strike group was assembled.
verdict_note: Commentary-tier claim with an unclear source; not used for any rating.

claim: Lithuania's border with Kaliningrad is calmer than Poland's
claimed_by: Lithuanian Defence Minister Robertas Kaunas (via LRT)
conflict: Consistent with Lithuania's interior minister saying earlier this week that the threat level had not changed, and with no reported incidents on the Lithuanian side; Poland remains on alert after the 3 November sighting.
verdict_note: Fits all public reporting; based on a short LRT item.

claim: Polish and allied intelligence warned of possible incursions by armed people from Kaliningrad in the first half of November
claimed_by: Donald Tusk; Tomasz Siemoniak; NATO commander Alexus Grynkewich (per Stars and Stripes)
conflict: Still no confirmed crossing attempt; Poland's operation continues until at least 8 November. Russia calls the warnings fake.
verdict_note: That the warnings were given is well established; whether an incursion was planned cannot be judged from public evidence.

claim: The Kraków shooting was a Russian-directed operation
claimed_by: Online speculation, and headlines framing the attack around Russian sabotage fears (e.g. FinChannel); no official
conflict: Polish officials say the suspect acted alone and point to radical, possibly far-right views; no foreign link, financing or network has been announced. The Russian embassy only reported that a Russian citizen was injured.
verdict_note: Nothing in the public evidence supports a Russian link; the investigation is still open.

claim: The Kraków gunman was driven by far-right extremist views
claimed_by: Interior Minister Marcin Kierwiński
conflict: Early findings only; the minister said this still needs investigation. Police dismissed reports of an accomplice and the defence ministry denied he was a soldier.
verdict_note: A preliminary official indication, not yet an established motive.

claim: The Coalition of the Willing drills show London and Paris seek Russia's military defeat
claimed_by: Maria Zakharova, Russian Foreign Ministry (via TASS)
conflict: Polish defence ministry details describe a post-hostilities deployment exercise, outside NATO and without combat or peacekeeping tasks.
verdict_note: The drills are real; the stated purpose contradicts Zakharova's description.

claim: Russia is not seeking good-faith talks in Abu Dhabi
claimed_by: ISW
conflict: Based on the make-up of Russia's delegation and its public rejection of security guarantees and a European role.
verdict_note: Consistent with Russia's on-the-record positions, but intent can only be judged after the talks.

claim: Polish and allied intelligence warned of possible incursions by armed people from Kaliningrad in the first half of November
claimed_by: Donald Tusk; Tomasz Siemoniak; NATO commander Alexus Grynkewich (per Stars and Stripes)
conflict: The operation reached its scheduled end date of 8 November with no confirmed crossing attempt; Russia calls the warnings fake.
verdict_note: That the warnings were given is well established; whether an incursion was planned cannot be judged from public evidence.

claim: The Kraków gunman was linked to Ukraine's International Legion or pro-Azov fighters
claimed_by: Russian Telegram channel Shot and pro-Kremlin accounts on X
conflict: Polish prosecutors identify a Polish citizen acting alone with far-right views; the patch cited is a generic design sold online, not a Ukrainian unit emblem.
verdict_note: Contradicted by official findings and by visual checks of the patch.

claim: The Kraków shooting was a Russian-directed operation
claimed_by: Online speculation and some headlines; no official
conflict: Prosecutors say evidence so far shows no one else was involved; officials name a far-right motive and no foreign link.
verdict_note: Still no public evidence of a Russian role; the investigation continues.

claim: The Kraków gunman acted from far-right extremist motives
claimed_by: Interior Minister Marcin Kierwiński; prosecutors
conflict: Some far-right politicians online dispute the label or claim left-wing or other motives, without evidence.
verdict_note: Now backed by prosecutors, who are treating the attack as terrorism; a final motive awaits the investigation.

claim: The disinformation surge after Kraków was coordinated, with Russian involvement
claimed_by: Deputy PM Krzysztof Gawkowski; NASK data (as reported by European Interest)
conflict: NASK found over 2,000 accounts, many automated, some with Russian markers; but domestic far-right figures pushed some of the same narratives, and no state actor has been formally named.
verdict_note: Coordinated amplification is well supported; Russian state direction is plausible but not proven publicly.

claim: Russia recruits Ukrainian refugees for sabotage in Europe; about 200 Russia-linked sabotage acts since 2022
claimed_by: Ukraine's Foreign Intelligence Service (via Ukrinform)
conflict: Fits European court cases and Lithuania's expulsion of three Ukrainians; the figures are given without a breakdown and come from a party to the war.
verdict_note: The pattern is well documented; the exact numbers are unconfirmed.

claim: Russia used the Oleshky truce to move over 1,000 troops and equipment to the Kherson left bank
claimed_by: Ukrainian military sources (via Militarnyi, Kyiv Post); noted by ISW
conflict: Not confirmed by Russia or independent imagery; ISW reports no major Russian assaults there yet.
verdict_note: A single-side claim; worth watching as a test of how Russia uses truces.

claim: Leaked Rosstat data show 390,000–450,000 Russians killed in the war
claimed_by: Hacker groups Belarus Cyber Partisans and Silent Crow; analysed by The Moscow Times
conflict: The two groups' totals differ by method; The Moscow Times verified a sample of names but not the full dataset; roughly in line with an earlier British estimate.
verdict_note: Plausible and partly checked, but the dataset's integrity cannot yet be confirmed.

claim: Foreign contingents in Ukraine would be military intervention and a foothold against Russia
claimed_by: Maria Zakharova, Russian Foreign Ministry
conflict: UK and French officials say the force would deploy only after a ceasefire, at Kyiv's request, with no combat or peacekeeping mandate and outside NATO.
verdict_note: Repeats earlier framing; the stated purpose of the force contradicts it.
